⧖ HELIX / LIGHTEXECUTABLE MODEL SPECIFICATION · v0.1
28 OCTOBER 2026 / IMPLEMENTED REFERENCE MODEL

The first helix–light experiment.

Purpose: connect a defined microscopic effective model to collective dynamics, a PTC-inspired clock representation and an optical response. This is a numerically tested illustrative model, not an ab initio calculation or a calibrated simulation of P1H11.

1. Experiment and state space

Prepare a stationary helical aggregate in its electronic ground state. Apply a linearly polarized Gaussian pulse. Evolve through excitation and subsequent environmental relaxation for 500 fs. Compare coupling, polarization, dephasing and prescribed site-energy modulation while retaining the same initial state and measurement definitions.

The Hilbert space has dimension 13: |0⟩ is the common ground state and |i⟩, i=1…12, is one localized electronic excitation at chromophore i. Double and higher excitations, vibrational quantum states, spin states and charge-transfer states are excluded. Consequently this model is intended for weak excitation; a drive slider does not establish the accuracy of the single-excitation approximation at high fluence.

ParameterReference value / meaning
Sites12 localized chromophores
GeometryRadius 1.2 nm; axial rise 0.36 nm per site; twist 55° per site
Electronic transition5.00 eV; identical bare sites
Coupling scale J₀0.025 eV; normalized dipole model
PulseCarrier 5.00 eV; envelope centre 80 fs; σ=25 fs; rotating-frame drive coefficient 0.006 eV; X polarization
Dephasing γφ0.003 fs⁻¹
Relaxation κ0.0005 fs⁻¹; lifetime 2,000 fs
Modulation amplitude A0 eV by default; adjustable 0–0.030 eV
Integration0–500 fs; RK4, Δt=0.5 fs; store every 2 fs
Energy–time conversionℏ=0.6582119569 eV fs

2. Geometry and couplings

θᵢ = i θ,   i = 0,…,11
rᵢ = (R cos θᵢ, R sin θᵢ, [i−(N−1)/2] a)
uᵢ = (−√0.75 sin θᵢ, √0.75 cos θᵢ, 0.5)
Jᵢⱼ = J₀ (r_nn / rᵢⱼ)³ [uᵢ·uⱼ − 3(uᵢ·r̂ᵢⱼ)(uⱼ·r̂ᵢⱼ)]

uᵢ is a unit transition-dipole direction. r_nn is the nearest-neighbour separation for the selected helix. Normalizing by r_nn preserves the chosen coupling scale when twist changes, so the twist slider is not a fixed-dipole-magnitude material prediction. J₀ is a phenomenological energy calibration; it is not inferred from a chemical transition moment. The point-dipole approximation can fail at close separation and should later be replaced by transition-density couplings where appropriate. The displayed hexagonal motifs are schematic chromophore glyphs, not an atomic reconstruction.

3. Hamiltonian and optical drive

H(t) = Σᵢ Δᵢ(t)|i⟩⟨i| + Σᵢ<ⱼ Jᵢⱼ(|i⟩⟨j|+|j⟩⟨i|)
       − V₀ f(t) Σᵢ (e·uᵢ)(|i⟩⟨0|+|0⟩⟨i|)
f(t) = exp[−(t−80 fs)² / (2 × (25 fs)²)]
Δᵢ(t) = A sin[2πt/(110+7i) fs + 1.618i], i=1,…,12

The rotating frame is defined by the laser carrier; bare detuning is zero. e is a unit vector along X, Y or Z. V₀ is the already reduced rotating-wave coupling energy. For a dipole magnitude μ and real laboratory field E₀ cos(ωt), V₀=μE₀/2 under this convention. We do not assign an optical intensity without μ. The optional modulation is a prescribed deterministic structural/environmental surrogate; it does not integrate nuclear forces, conserve an explicit bath energy or represent sampled thermal molecular dynamics.

4. Environment and evolution

dρ/dt = −i[H,ρ]/ℏ + Σᵢ D[√γφ |i⟩⟨i|]ρ + Σᵢ D[√κ |0⟩⟨i|]ρ
D[L]ρ = LρL† − ½(L†Lρ + ρL†L)
ρ(0) = |0⟩⟨0|

The bath is Markovian and site-local. Intersite coherences decay at γφ+κ in the absence of the Hamiltonian; ground–site coherences decay at (γφ+κ)/2. Excited populations decay at κ. No temperature is implied by these phenomenological rates, and detailed-balance thermalization among exciton eigenstates is not implemented. All decay is represented as return to the ground state; no radiative branching ratio is specified, so it is not a fluorescence calculation.

RK4 does not guarantee positivity at arbitrary step sizes. The specified reference step is checked for convergence and positivity. Density matrices are not clipped or renormalized to hide numerical errors.

Clock rings are arranged on a common display circle. Their radius is normalized to the largest coherence amplitude in the current frame. The density-matrix colour scale is also normalized per frame, with the scale printed below it. Clock layout and matrix brightness are representations, not extra physical dimensions. Site selection links the molecular view and density matrix.

6. Optical output

Diagonalize the undriven, unmodulated excited block. For normalized eigenvector vₐ, transition strength Sₐ=|Σᵢ(e·uᵢ)vᵢₐ|². Plot Σₐ Sₐ η²/[(E−Eₐ)²+η²], with η=0.012 eV, over 4.8–5.2 eV. The plot is a relative linear-absorption proxy normalized by its maximum. The broadening is chosen for visualization and is not derived from the Lindblad rates. It represents the initial static Hamiltonian associated with the same run, not an instantaneous spectrum. It excludes orientational averaging, absolute absorption coefficients, CD and fluorescence.

7. Microscopic-to-PTC connection and corrections

This version implements only the first explicit map: density matrix → optical-coherence phases/amplitudes → clock geometry. Optical phases depend on the laser reference and basis convention. We do not identify these clock loops with physical closed nanowires, nor claim persistent subharmonic order or a six-/twelve-dimensional PTC theorem.

  • Topology must be calculated from specified connectivity: an open helix is not a closed loop; a tree has no graph cycles.
  • For ordinary boundary/coboundary maps, ∂²=δ²=0. Future mismatch diagnostics must use constraint residuals or a separately defined connection curvature.
  • Homology and cohomology dimensions for the same finite complex over a field agree. Their difference cannot serve as an independent physical driving force.
  • Unitary exp(−iγδ†δ) alone cannot reduce the expectation of δ†δ. Healing needs an explicit dissipative/control mechanism.
  • A single global phase has no density-matrix effect. Optical control must use relative phases between specified modes.
  • Phase alignment is distinct from entanglement and time-crystal order. Mean-field condensate fields cannot by themselves certify arbitrary many-body entanglement.
  • Any polariton module must state its applicability, loss, reservoir depletion and saturation; repulsive nonlinearity alone does not establish a stable 3D bright soliton.

8. Numerical acceptance

The shipped reference passes trace preservation, Hermiticity, half-step convergence, zero-drive stationarity, closed-system purity, oscillator-strength sum rule, analytic decay-generator agreement, density-matrix positivity, and agreement with independently implemented SciPy DOP853 dynamics. Machine-readable results. The default density-matrix error against SciPy is approximately 1.28×10⁻⁸.

Reproduce from the source checkout: node tests.mjs
python validate_reference.pyPython requires NumPy and SciPy. These are numerical checks, not experimental confirmation. Parameter extremes should receive new convergence checks before research use.

9. Finite roadmap

  1. Current milestone: a complete helix–light experiment with numerical validation and linked views.
  2. Material calibration: verified molecular identity, structures, transition energies/densities, dipole magnitudes and existing optical data. Maintain parameter uncertainty.
  3. Structure and feedback: import molecular trajectories; calculate couplings; then add justified excited-state forces. Compare prescribed versus self-consistent dynamics.
  4. PTC correspondence: test recurrences, phase stability, drive-relative subharmonic response, connectivity and mapping non-uniqueness. Add topology only with explicit complexes.
  5. Magnetic and RF: introduce supported spin/electric/dielectric pathways and matched heating controls; validate isolated limiting cases first.
  6. Collective light–matter: add photon modes and reservoirs where strong coupling/condensation is justified; derive optical output and measurement uncertainty.
  7. Hierarchical networks: scale assemblies and field/material sweeps, tracking approximation errors; distinguish independent parameter runs from physically coupled channels.

Research reference: Singh et al., A 1024-channel room-temperature polyatomic time-crystal architecture for self-operating quantum computing, AIP Advances 16, 105011 (2026). This implementation is a corrected minimal research model inspired by the discussed questions; it does not reproduce the paper’s unavailable simulator or its numerical figures.
